summary: Will Johnson reconnected after a ~1.5–2 year hiatus to get back onto TeamBuildr OS for his gym, Grind Time, in the Whittier, CA area. The rep walked through several new OS features and proposed a 12-month monthly-pay contract specific to OS (separate from his existing Strength subscription). Will expressed readiness to sign the contract and move forward, with his only pending item being sorting out a business email address.

name: Jesse Cook and Luke Martin
buying_signals: Asked detailed questions about payment flows, membership billing cycles, and how clients would onboard — clearly envisioning implementation
Proactively mapped his three service lines (small group, personal training, team training) to OS features during the demo
Asked about staff roles and what his coaches would see — thinking through internal rollout
Confirmed preference to drive purchases through OS ('I'd rather pay the 2% and have it done like that')
Asked about parent vs. athlete app experience — planning client communication strategy
Expressed desire for a centralized hub to replace Google Calendar, QuickBooks invoicing, and text message scheduling
objections: Large team training invoices (e.g. $9,000 for 48-session package) may not suit credit card payment via OS — Jesse intends to continue invoicing those clients through QuickBooks in installments
Wants to maintain QuickBooks as the accounting source of truth; OS revenue numbers may not align perfectly with his accountant's records
summary: This was an OS demo call with Jesse Cook, owner of a hockey-focused sports performance facility. Jesse is an existing TeamBuildr Strength user of ~6 years exploring OS to solve scheduling chaos, session tracking for packages, and client self-booking. He was highly engaged throughout, asking detailed questions about memberships, packages, payment flows, staff roles, and app experience — strong fit and clear intent to move forward.
